visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a middle-aged male presenter wearing glasses and a black shirt, pointing his finger upwards against a studio backdrop featuring a bookshelf. The lighting is warm and directional, highlighting the speaker's expressive face and gestures as he initiates a direct-to-camera address. (2) A digital screen capture of the Taipei Astronomical Museum website appears, displaying Chinese text titled "Astronomical News." The layout is clean and white, showing a headline about a second moon orbiting Earth in late 2024, providing a formal informational contrast to the previous live-action segment. (3) The presenter returns to the frame, using wide hand movements to describe the size and trajectory of asteroid 2024 PT5. He remains in the same indoor setting, with the bookshelf and a small skeleton model visible in the blurred background, maintaining a consistent professional atmosphere. (4) A technical diagram illustrates the path of a celestial body entering Earth's atmosphere. Labels in Traditional Chinese identify outer space, the atmosphere, and the resulting meteor and meteorite stages. The colors are dark blue and white, with simple geometric lines showing orbital trajectories. (5) The speaker introduces a small whiteboard with three blue sticky notes. He pulls the notes away one by one to reveal the labels "Comet," "Asteroid," and "Man-made Object." His actions are precise, and his facial expressions convey academic curiosity as he explains the categorization of near-Earth objects. (6) A cinematic simulation depicts an astronaut on the moon's surface witnessing a large celestial impact. The scene is dominated by dark, desaturated tones and green lens flares, creating a dramatic, high-contrast visual that contrasts with the brightly lit studio scenes shown earlier. (7) An English-language scientific article and a newspaper clipping are overlaid on the screen. The headlines discuss the moon-rock origin of the small asteroid visitor. The text is crisp and clear, presented against a gray background to emphasize the evidence-based nature of the discussion. (8) The final sequence shows a high-detail close-up of the moon's cratered surface followed by the presenter wrapping up his talk. He maintains his seated position behind a black table, gesturing towards the camera as the video concludes in the studio setting.
